title: Blocked Category Trending
exclusions: Covers web traffic that goes through the Secure Access or Umbrella web gateway. Traffic from devices that bypass the gateway is not seen.
evidence: Monthly export of the 30-day chart with notes on any category that changed sharply and the reason.

controlTest.positiveScenario: From a test client using the Secure Access or Umbrella web gateway, browse to Cisco's documented test site `www.examplemalwaredomain.com`. After the next S3 sync the request is in `index=sse` with `action=Blocked`, and the day's count for its security category increases by one.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Browse to `www.cisco.com` from the same client. The request is logged as Allowed and no blocked-category count changes.

dataSources: `index=sse sourcetype=cisco:cloud_security:proxy` (or `cisco:umbrella:proxy` on older Umbrella exports) from the Secure Access or Umbrella S3 log bucket, read by the Cisco Secure Access Add-on (7569). One event per web request through the secure web gateway with `action`, `url`, `url_domain`, `category`, `blocked_category`, `user`, `identities`, `src_ip`, `bytes_in`, `bytes_out`, `http_method`, and `status`, tagged `web` and `proxy` for the CIM Web data model.
app: Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk ([Splunkbase 7569](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7569)), which reads Cisco Secure Access and Cisco Umbrella logs from the S3 log bucket and maps the web proxy log to the CIM Web data model. The companion Cisco Secure Access App (Splunkbase 5558) adds dashboards.
spl:
index=sse sourcetype IN ("cisco:cloud_security:proxy", "cisco:umbrella:proxy")
| eval action=lower(action)
| where action="blocked"
| eval block_category=coalesce(nullif(blocked_category, ""), category)
| makemv delim="," block_category
| timechart span=1d count by block_category limit=15 useother=true
description: Charts web requests blocked by the Cisco Secure Access or Umbrella secure web gateway per day, split by the category that caused the block, so shifts in what is being blocked stand out.
value: A category that suddenly climbs, such as malware or newly seen domains, is an early sign of an infection or a phishing wave; one that climbs after a policy change shows a rule that is blocking work. The daily trend shows both without anyone reading individual block events.
implementation: Collect the Secure Access or Umbrella web proxy log with the Cisco Secure Access Add-on (7569) into `index=sse`. Show as a 30-day dashboard panel, and alert when a security category doubles day over day.
visualization: Stacked column chart of daily blocks by category over 30 days, plus a table of the top blocked domains for the selected category.
cimSpl:
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web where Web.action="blocked" by _time span=1d Web.category
| rename Web.category as category
| timechart span=1d sum(count) as blocks by category limit=15 useother=true
dataModelAcceleration: Enable acceleration on the CIM Web data model over `index=sse` before using the tstats variant.

references.title: Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 7569)
Cisco Umbrella: Log Management and Amazon S3 log export
Cisco Umbrella: Manage Content Categories and Security Categories
Splunk: Integrated Enterprise Value for Cisco data (supported source types)

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Policy changes** — adding a category to a block policy makes it jump overnight. Annotate the chart with policy change dates from the Secure Access audit log.

2. **Multi-category destinations** — Secure Access assigns several categories to one destination; `blocked_category` is used when present so the chart shows the category that actually triggered the block.

**Suppression:** none; this is a trend view. Alerts should exclude content categories that the policy team already reviews.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 7569) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Inputs Data Manager that reads the S3 bucket.
• Log export to Amazon S3 enabled in the Secure Access or Umbrella dashboard (Admin > Log Management), either a Cisco-managed bucket or your own, with the access key and secret for Splunk.
• An index for Secure Access and Umbrella data (this page uses `index=sse`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the network security team.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In the add-on create an S3 modular input for the web proxy log path with the bucket name, region, access key, and secret, and set the index to `sse`.
• Logs reach S3 in batches, so events usually arrive in Splunk 10 to 15 minutes after the request. `action` is logged as Allowed or Blocked (ALLOWED or BLOCKED in some exports); the searches lowercase it.
• Check the fields this search needs: run `index=sse sourcetype="cisco:cloud_security:proxy" | stats count by action` over 1 day and confirm both values appear.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=sse sourcetype IN ("cisco:cloud_security:proxy", "cisco:umbrella:proxy")
| eval action=lower(action)
| where action="blocked"
| eval block_category=coalesce(nullif(blocked_category, ""), category)
| makemv delim="," block_category
| timechart span=1d count by block_category limit=15 useother=true
```

Understanding this SPL
• The first line reads the web proxy log from both the current Secure Access source type and the older Umbrella one.
• `lower(action)` makes the comparison work whichever case the export uses.
• `block_category` prefers `blocked_category`, the category that triggered the block, and falls back to the full `category` list; `makemv` splits a comma-separated list so each category is counted.
• `timechart ... limit=15 useother=true` keeps the chart readable by grouping small categories into OTHER.

Accelerated variant over the CIM data model:
```spl
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web where Web.action="blocked" by _time span=1d Web.category
| rename Web.category as category
| timechart span=1d sum(count) as blocks by category limit=15 useother=true
```
• The tstats variant counts blocked requests by `Web.category` on the accelerated Web data model; it uses `category` because the CIM model has no blocked-category field.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Secure Access dashboard (or the Umbrella dashboard) under Reporting > Activity Search, filtered to Web and the same time range: the totals there should match the totals here within the S3 delivery delay.
• Pick one day and one category from the chart and confirm the count against Activity Search filtered to Blocked and that category.
• Run `index=sse sourcetype="cisco:cloud_security:proxy" | timechart span=1h count` over 7 days; gaps longer than an hour point to S3 input failures.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Place on the network security dashboard with a 30-day range.
• Alert daily when a security category (Malware, Phishing, Command and Control, Cryptomining) at least doubles against the previous 7-day average.
• Review the chart in the monthly policy meeting.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No proxy events and S3 access errors (403 AccessDenied) in the add-on log: the access key cannot read the bucket or the region is wrong.
• Proxy events missing while DNS events arrive: the Secure Web Gateway is not enabled for those identities, or the S3 input path points at the DNS folder only.
• Events arrive hours late: the input polling interval is long, or the bucket path prefix is wrong and the input scans the whole bucket.
• The tstats variant returns nothing while the raw search works: the Web data model is not accelerated over `index=sse`, or the `cim_Web_indexes` macro does not include it.
grandmaExplanation: We chart which kinds of websites our web filter blocks each day, so a sudden rise in dangerous sites or a rule blocking real work stands out.
